security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel (S-mode) sets a bit in sstateen* to grant U-mode access to extension state, but does not context-switch that state between user threads — e.g., enabling JVT (Zcmt), FCSR (Zfinx), or custom state (C bit) in sstateen0, then calling cpu_switch() in swtch.S without saving/restoring the corresponding CSR or state. Additionally, if OpenSBI (M-mode) does not set bit 63 of mstateen0 before booting FreeBSD, the kernel cannot access sstateen0 at all, and if OpenSBI fails to zero-initialize writable bits of sstateen* before entering S-mode, FreeBSD inherits stale enable values.
security_spec.summary: Smstateen defines per-extension state-enable bits to prevent covert channels; FreeBSD must either context-switch all state corresponding to enabled sstateen* bits, or risk cross-thread information leakage through unswapped extension state
